NAME SWEEP LOG — Open Library search-inside, 2026-09-06
=======================================================
p_430 asks for the camp's PEOPLE to be run against the Internet Archive book corpus, and CLAUDE.md's
Phase 2 mandate says to "log every search attempted and its result (even null results) so the same
ground is not re-covered." This file is that log. It is the authoritative record of which names have
been run; if a name is not here, it has not been swept.

Method: bare-name phrase query against https://openlibrary.org/search/inside.json (contract at
f_4933). Where a name returns many hits, they were read far enough to say whose they are.


THE CAMP'S OWN NAME — ALTERNATIVE SPELLINGS
--------------------------------------------
  "Kanawana"        76 items   (swept earlier 2026-09-06; the enumeration is in p_430)
  "Camp Kanawana"    8 items   (the phrase every earlier pass used, and the reason this was late)
  "Kamp Kanawana"   13 items   ** TWO OF THEM IN NEITHER LIST ABOVE ** — the DLB entry on Stuart
                               McLean (f_4949) and the American Camp Association textbook (f_4950)
  "Kanawanna"        0
  "Lac Kanawana"     0
  "Kanawana, Que"    0
  "Lake Kanawana"    1 item    — the Stuart McLean passage already read (f_4941)

CONCLUSION: run BOTH "Kanawana" and "Kamp Kanawana". The other spellings are dead and need not be
run again.


PEOPLE — SWEPT 2026-09-06
--------------------------

  Lemuel P. Ereaux ........ 0 hits.  NULL.
  Lemuel Ereaux ........... 0 hits.  NULL.
  Allan B. Cornell ........ 0 hits.  NULL.
  R.H. Hanagan ............ 0 hits.  NULL.
  Philip G. Paterson ...... 0 hits.  NULL.
  G.D. Brandon ............ 0 hits.  NULL.

  Edwin M. Crawford ....... 65 hits, EVERY ONE an American university-relations officer of the 1980s
                            and 90s (Auburn, Ohio State, CASE). None is Kanawana's 1922 Junior
                            Section Director. A common name in a large corpus costs reading and
                            returns nothing; do not re-run it bare.

  W.J. Holliday ........... 243 hits, essentially all an Indianapolis art collector and an
                            Indianapolis steel company of the same name. Do not re-run bare; pair
                            with "Montreal" or "Y.M.C.A." if it is run again at all.

  Johnston W. Abraham ..... 1 hit, AND IT IS AN OPEN LEAD, NOT A FINDING. The Union List of
                            Manuscripts in Canadian Repositories, supplement 1979-1980 (Public
                            Archives Canada, 1982), leaf 288: "... Annual reports, correspondence,
                            membership lists, memorabilia and press clippings. Ref./Réf.: P.A.C.,
                            MG 28 (I 280). Provenance: Johnston W. Abraham, DeWittville, Que."
                            The fonds runs 1917-1978, 10 cm. THE COLLECTION'S NAME WAS NOT
                            RECOVERED: the Union List is set in two columns, the OCR interleaves
                            them, and six attempts to walk backwards to the heading ran into
                            entries for the Sherbrooke and District University Women's Club on both
                            sides. Nor is it established that this is Kanawana's Johnston W. Abraham
                            (Business Manager from about 1914, documented in his ninth year in
                            1922) rather than another man of the same name.
                            WHY IT IS WORTH KEEPING ANYWAY: it is a precise archival reference at
                            Library and Archives Canada — MG 28 (I 280) — which a person with
                            ordinary browser access resolves in one lookup, and this environment
                            cannot, the LAC gateway returning HTTP 403 (see p_428). Tracked there.

  F. H. Spinney ........... 12 hits. FOUR are a different F. H. Spinney of Hudson, New Hampshire,
                            a volunteer variable-star observer in Harvard College Observatory annual
                            reports 1913-1916. ONE IS HIM: "School: a magazine devoted to elementary
                            and secondary education", vol. 1 (Toronto, 1912-13) — "F. H. SPINNEY,
                            Principal Alexandra School, Montreal", author of the eight-part column
                            "In the Little Red Schoolhouse", with a second series commissioned.
                            f_4958, and p_432 for the rest of that run.

  Hay Finlay .............. 19 hits, four items. One is a 1769 Scottish tenant farmer ("HAY, FINLAY,
                            joint tenant farmer in Easter Croftmartage"), one a comparative
                            psychology study citing an unrelated pair of researchers. TWO ARE HIM:
                            a McGill history (Nurmberg1970) which has McGill "engage Mr. Hay Finlay
                            as the gymnastic coach", and "The McGill You Knew: An Anthology of
                            Memories, 1920-1960" (1975), which gives him as gymnastics and soccer
                            coach and has him and Van Wagner developing Camp Nominingue, "known as
                            'Camp McGill' to all the residents of the area". f_4959.
                            NOTE: the Nurmberg1970 item was NOT walked and may hold more.

TWO PIECES OF ADVICE FROM THE SIX NAMES ALREADY RUN. Names that are common in English (Crawford,
Holliday) return hundreds of hits about other people and should be paired with "Montreal",
"Y.M.C.A." or "Kanawana" from the start. Names that are rare (Ereaux, Hanagan, Brandon with
initials) return zero, and a zero here is a fact about a book corpus and not about the world — these
men are in city directories, church records and newspapers that the Internet Archive's book
collection does not contain.

AND THE YIELD IS NOT PROPORTIONAL TO THE NAMES. Of the first nine names swept, six returned nothing
usable, one returned an open archival lead, and two opened real biographies — one of which
(Hay Finlay) turned out to answer a standing open question in another article using facts this
project had already had for weeks. There is no way to tell in advance which is which.
